title: security: rbac-v2 enforce KMS region pinning + audit-logging hardening for Private deployments
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require strict data residency guarantees and cryptographic separation for customer keys. This PR enforces KMS region pinning at the RBAC v2 layer, elevates audit logging for all key-binding and policy changes, and hardens the migration path for existing tenants. Changes include a policy-enforcement hook in the RBAC engine, richer audit events emitted to the audit pipeline, migration tooling to backfill existing resources, and docs/installer updates for Private/VPC installs. Checklist: - [x] RBAC enforcement hook implemented and unit tested - [x] Audit event schema extended and downstream mapping updated - [x] Migration job implemented with dry-run and apply modes - [x] Integration tests for Private installer and KMS residency - [x] Docs for operators and upgrade notes - [x] Security scan and threat model review Outcomes: RBAC now rejects cross-region KMS bindings unless explicitly allowed by a tenancy override flag (opt-in for legacy accounts). Audit logs now include prev/new key_region, actor, request_id, and policy_rule_id fields and are emitted synchronously for control-plane actions to ensure traceability during upgrades. Rollback: migration tool supports revert for apply runs and the enforcement hook has a feature flag to disable enforcement immediately if rollout causes regressions. Backwards compatibility: no public API surface changes for external customers; upgrade path documented.

notes_for_oncall: If customers report key_binding rejections after upgrade, disable enforcement via feature flag and run migration in dry-run to inspect mismatches. Contact security@redwood.com for incident escalation.
